rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5: "This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves." — body grep for the §1 list returns 1 hit, all inside the maintainer cut at L66+ returns none. Harm §1 prevents: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader; present here, the adverb is doing no work the sentence needs.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; it is the only thing "crucially" is propping up.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban in any curriculum/training surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L11: "Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session." — 1 body hit on the ritual/ceremony grep. Harm: the exact Scrum-ceremony register the word ban exists to keep out of an exercise page, and the file is an exercise, which is the sanctioned word.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the line, or say "a move you repeat" if the repetition claim is wanted.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L49: "This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14." — 1 body hit on the transition-verb grep and 1 on the bare-date grep, both on this line, above the L66 cut. Tense test: a reader who never saw the previous version loses nothing. Harm: changelog in student prose, present and unambiguous — this is the journey, not a dated provenance header in a maintainer block.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the line outright; git carries the history.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to the AE101 quintet line is L5, "This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves." — grand without content, but it is charged under §1/§26 and the rest of the body holds Boris-direct instruction plus one Rory reframe at L57. No poster wrapper: grep for **Remember / Hold onto / Keep in mind / Never forget returns 0 in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise body, not an article draft handed to the maintainer for rewrite.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body names no practitioner; grep for Antti|the creator|the author|course creator returns 0 above the cut. Timing sub-rule satisfied: line 3 is a bare "**Time:** 20 minutes." with blank lines either side, total only, no phase breakdown.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L24: "At this point the student should notice the test is still red." — 1 body hit on the-student grep, above the cut, and it is not the Connections room-harvest carve-out. Harm: third-person teacher framing leaking into student-facing prose; a student reads a sentence about somebody else.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast to second person and to an action: "The test is still red."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only candidate is "connector" at L43. The maintainer block carries a standing accept-note at L72 ruling it assumed-known for the engineer audience and saying findings on it are not to be re-filed. No other body term appears solely in the maintainer or backing blocks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L37: "There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way." — "no penalty" is a named flag phrase in the rule, and the second clause repeats the first. Harm: a senior engineer asks why the author is telling them this is OK; the reassurance signals the optional beat needed defending.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; L39 already frames the push-back as worth doing on its own terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No user-supplied verbal frame is being captured into a reference artefact here; the one maintainer-attested frame is already verbatim in the backing block at L125.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner is named in body prose at all, so the cap cannot fire.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L57 opens "The ticket is one instance." before the "Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered" reach, so the boundary sits in the same bullet rather than being bolted on as a hedge. See notes for a rule question about the stance clause at L134 pointing at a third bullet this section does not have.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for vendor|marketing|not theoretical|grounded in actual|real practitioners returns 0 in the body region. Closest is L43 "it pays back on every session after this one" — a payoff in the student's own currency, not a positioning defence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "reverse-engineer" is the module's own move, earned at L13 ("**The point:** the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules") before its operational use at L33. No LLM-internal vocabulary in lead-ins; "LLM" at L57 is commonly-held AE101 working vocabulary per §4.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest closer is L64, "The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session." — both referents resolve to concrete nouns named in the same sentence, and no bypass-the-agent punchline appears.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The **What happened:** block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The recap at L60-64 runs the three moves: count plus noun ("Two things came out of one ticket"), one qualifier on ownership ("the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along"), and a destination ("The field rules stay in the scrollback"). Past tense throughout, 2 sentences, no replay.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for bark|order|command|whip|boss|scold|force|drag returns 1 body hit, L43 "one command per tracker" — the noun, not a verb aimed at the agent. Body verbs are ask, tell, push back, drop.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest is "## Anything can be reverse-engineered" at L55 — the section body does assert exactly that, and L57 immediately bounds it with "The ticket is one instance." No "other X" header with no named primary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest is the deictic drumroll shape at L5, "This is crucially the step that…", which is charged once under §1 and §26 rather than three times here. No bold-label echo, no empty "X, not Y" negation, no citation duplication in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L62 "Two things came out of one ticket:" sits above its own two-item list, but this is the §16 move-1 count-plus-noun shape the recap block is specified to use ("One plan, two reads"). L33 "propose five bug rules" is content, not a tally of visible items.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L57 "Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM" carries a superlative, and the backing block records it as a deliberate vision-grade stance at L132-135 with the boundary held in the same bullet. Filing REVISE here would falsify a maintainer-attested frame; raised as a rule question in notes instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No claim is being re-verified in this pass, and this bench fixture is a copy rather than a corpus member, so no sibling body states its source ids.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Governs sweep procedure, not the body under judgement; this fire is a single target with a brief derived at dispatch time.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: One doc per scarce-attention audience; delta-only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise page for the student, not an artifact authored for trainers, execs or sponsors.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trainer-facing text is self-contained.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No trainer-facing surface here; the repo paths in the file all sit below the L66 maintainer cut, where the reader is a maintainer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest is L53, "Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?" — the observation named is the existing ticket comments, an external artifact that can come back negative, not the close-out judging itself.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest is L24, "At this point the student should notice the test is still red." — third-person, charged under check_writing §7, but it asserts no deficiency and pegs no ability tier. No "at your scale" / "for a beginner" phrasing anywhere in body; no identity criterion split.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "connector" (L43) and "tracker" are assumed-known for the AE101 engineer audience, and the maintainer accept-note at L72 rules exactly that and says not to re-file. "reverse-engineer" is earned at L13 before use.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 engineer audience; the SVP-marketing flinch test is the Agents 101 / Claude Basics default and does not govern this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for memory|context window returns 0 in the body region; neither term is used, so there is nothing to blur.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two recoveries sit in body and both pass the base test of plausible failure plus non-obvious rescue: L18 (no ticket for this bug, the agent offers to create one) and L30 (no ticket of your own, any other real ticket works). The tracker-unreachable branch is correctly routed below the cut at L92.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The three prompts are registry-resolved markers ({{prompt:close-the-ticket-N}}); their bodies live in check_prompts scope, not in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise file with no Debrief or compound beat; the maintainer block at L70 states the fold belongs to compound-and-close.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body holds M1 register throughout — ship-and-close, warm and concrete. The one forward reach, L64 "The next exercise sweeps this whole session", names the neighbour without borrowing its mood.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The register beat this rule cites as its own precedent now carries actor, mechanism and addressee: L53 "If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it." L45 hands the write to the agent and asks it to report back, rather than asking the student to diff.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Governs self-study simulation scoring, not an in-class exercise body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for that callout shape returns 0 in body; the file carries no research callout and no inline citation at all.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every forcing function is a prompt to the agent (L22, L35, L47). The only student-side act is pasting a ticket link at L17, which is input to the conversation, not an editor or terminal primitive.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No CLAUDE.md is named in the body region; the one mention is at L104, below the maintainer cut, and it is qualified there as ./CLAUDE.local.md.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: awk over lines 1-65 for the em-dash character returns 0 hits. Sentences run short; the longest, L28, splits on a colon rather than a dash.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The four acting sections lead with verbs: "Read the ticket for your bug", "Read the conventions off the ticket", "Write the close-out and send it", "Double-check the voice". "Anything can be reverse-engineered" (L55) is an understanding beat and "What happened" (L60) is the canonical recap name.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The single link at L43 reads "[MCP and connectors]" — the target page's title, not its filename and not a backticked path. No ordinal cross-references in body: no "Step N" or "Phase N" appears above the cut.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "rules" is the only contested word in body, and it is consistently the team's bug rules read off the tracker (L9, L31, L64). No rules file is authored in this exercise (maintainer block, L70), so the first-authored-write moment this rule guards does not occur here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The split holds: capability/thinking takes LLM (L57), the acting steps take the agent (L29, L58), invocation takes Claude (L33, L45). The backing block at L125 records the same split as deliberate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5: "…the step that changes how the run behaves." Noun-run for the agent's sitting, which is the banned form; it is not a test, CI or eval execution, not a quote, and not a path name. Harm: it competes with "session", the word the same file uses correctly at L11, L43 and L64.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: The line is already owed a cut under §1 and §26; if any of it survives, say "session".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for tomorrow|overnight|this morning|tonight|yesterday|last night returns 0 in the body region. Closest temporal phrase is L43 "on every session after this one" — session-relative, which is the sanctioned replacement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No self-aware pedagogy header and no contemplative-pause prefix. Closest is L24 "At this point the student should notice…", which narrates rather than instructs, and is charged under check_writing §7.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No body beat restates an agent output: every section either sets up a prompt or steers what came back. The one promptless section, "Anything can be reverse-engineered" (L55), carries no LO and no decision to declare.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: .md is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The only artifact filename in body is L58, "Extract a `.md` file." — the default, and no .txt or .docx appears.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5: "This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves." Nothing downstream is made better by it — L7 already says what the student does and L13 already carries the point in the "**The point:**" widget. Deletion test: L4 and L7 join cleanly. Harm: a second, vaguer point statement two lines above the real one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L53 follows the close-out print but names a specific criterion (does it sound like the comments already on the ticket) and a follow-on move (tell Claude which line), so it is the carve-out, not a bare "read it".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L64 "The next exercise sweeps this whole session." takes an exercise as subject, but it is the check_writing §16 move-3 landing ("what reads it next"), which that rule specifies by name. Flagging it would break the recap shape rather than fix a leak; the sentence sells nothing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No per-module operational setting (thinking effort, model, mode tag, worktree path) applies to this exercise; the maintainer block at L83 routes delivery architecture to training-architecture.md.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body reaches for house vocabulary rather than synonyms: session, scrollback, close-out, push back, rules. Closest miss is "the run" at L5, charged under §21b.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for typing |type in|say to Claude|tell it to returns 0 in body. Directions to the agent take the prompt-noun or the plain ask: "Ask Claude to write the close-out" (L45), "tell Claude which line" (L53).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L43 states the outcome and hands the detail to a reference page — "Adding a connector is one command per tracker" — rather than writing an install recipe. The maintainer block at L74 records that choice deliberately.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only two candidates. L64 is the sanctioned §16 destination move. L5 fails the deletion test and is charged under §26 rather than doubled here. No arc-positioning prose about later modules.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Four sharing strategies (Agents 101 M7 canonical) — use verbatim.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Agents 101 M7 canonical text; this is an AE101 M1 exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Agents 101 M2+ Debrief — canonical shape.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Agents 101 Debrief shape; this file is an AE101 exercise with no Debrief section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No scaffold ships with the exercise. All three artifacts (bug rules, close-out note, ticket update) are produced through prompts at L22, L35 and L47.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 M1 target is earned trust, and the body holds it: the student reads their own tracker and pushes back on what the agent proposes (L39). The planted reassurance at L37 pulls against it, charged under check_writing §9.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned word in student-facing body: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader, and the adverb props up a sentence carrying no content.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Hard-banned word on a curriculum surface; imports Scrum-ceremony register into the exercise page, and exercise is the sanctioned noun.
findings.fix: Cut the line, or write "a move you repeat" if the repetition claim is wanted.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Changelog in student prose. A reader who never saw the previous version loses nothing; the transition verb and bare date are the journey, not a maintainer provenance header.
findings.fix: Delete the line; git carries the history.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher framing in student-facing body: the student reads a sentence about somebody else, and the delivery mechanic leaks above the maintainer cut.
findings.fix: Recast as second person and as state: "The test is still red."

todos.note: "There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way." — over-hedge; "no penalty" is a named flag phrase and the second clause repeats the first. Cut it; L39 already carries the case for doing the push-back.
"how the run behaves" — noun-run for the agent's sitting is banned in student-facing body. The line is already owed a cut; if anything survives, say "session".
The whole of L5 is NVA: L7 states what the student does and L13 carries the point. Deletion test passes, L4 and L7 join cleanly.

notes: Brief built cleanly (rules kept=129 dropped=0), so the five compendiums were not read in full. Body region = lines 1-65; maintainer cut at L66; no fenced code blocks. Rule question, not filed as a finding: the stance clause at L134 says the "Anything can be reverse-engineered" slogan "carries its boundary in the third bullet" and that a judge should "read the third bullet before flagging", but that section (L55-58) has only two bullets. The boundary is in fact carried by the opening clause of the first bullet, "The ticket is one instance." Either the stance clause is a stale keep-note owing a rewrite under check_writing §3, or a third bullet was cut without the note following it. Out-of-lane observations for other classes: none.
